label: OnDeploy() handler
type: the third Eventing Function entry point: runs once when a Function is deployed or resumed, before any mutation is processed. A member of eventing-handler-family. NOT triggered by a document mutation like OnUpdate/OnDelete, and NOT re-run on every resume from a checkpoint - it runs once per deploy/resume event itself.
folded_spellings_note: eventing:ondeploy-handler was round 8's independent minting of this exact concept (2 files, cloud only); this round's own eventing-lifecycle.md/eventing-Terminologies.md/eventing-language-constructs.md minted eventing:on-deploy-handler (3 files, server only) without seeing it. A pure hyphen-only difference is a punctuation variant of this record's own id, not a defensible alternative name, so verify-registry-ids.py correctly refused it as an alias - rewritten instead via normalise-ids.py's ID_RENAMES table (the same treatment already applied to onupdate-handler/ondelete-handler in round 8), which folded it here automatically once no corpus occurrence remained. Caught by recurrence.py --variants (a hyphen-only difference), unlike the timer-callback fork in the family record, which the same tool misses entirely because it isn't a spelling variant at all.
evidence: The `OnDeploy` handler runs once when an Eventing function is deployed or resumed, before any mutations are processed.
The OnDeploy entry point must complete execution, from start to end, within the specified timeout period.
OnDeploy Timeout defines the maximum duration allowed for an Eventing Function to complete its initialization during deployment or resumption.
relates_to_competency_question: Can a Function run setup logic exactly once, before it starts processing mutations?
